title: Slow peg oscillation and lead-lag batch stalls (scratch)
content:
Notes to self: intermittent throughput regressions observed over last 48h. Symptoms not classic cbatch oscillation — instead we see a slow (~30–90s) peg/throughput drop that partially recovers, then drops again. Feels like a lead/lag between feeder (request multiplexer) and executor (batch consumer) where prefill timing misaligns with KV cache warmup, producing micro-starvation windows that cascade.

High-level timeline:
- 2025-11-01 10:12 PDT: first automated alert (p99 latency > target) on a hosted cluster.
- 2025-11-01 10:12–10:25: repeated ~40s troughs in token/sec; CPU/GPU utilization dips only on executor side.
- 2025-11-02 03:40 PDT: attempted config change (increase prefill timeout from 30ms -> 60ms) in canary; no stable improvement.

Repro notes (local canary):
- Traffic generator: loadtest-evgen (same prompt mix as production).
- Repro command (k8s pod exec into feeder):
  kubectl exec -it feeder-canary-7fd9c -- /bin/bash -c "./gen-traffic --rps 400 --seqdist short --seed 42"
- Watch window: token throughput from /debug/telemetry/throughput (scraped every 1s). Typical pattern:
  10:02:04  tokens/s: 2800
  10:02:12  tokens/s: 1200  <-- drop
  10:02:43  tokens/s: 2900  <-- recovery
  10:03:15  tokens/s: 900   <-- deeper drop

Commands used to triage:
- kubectl logs -f executor-xxx | ts | grep -i "batch" -- showed continuous small warnings about prefill-timeouts
- curl http://executor-canary/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > prof.pb
- pprof --text prof.pb | head -n 40  (no obvious hot CPU functions other than KV::Lookup and Batcher::pop)
- ./kv-warmup-stats --dump  -> cold hit rate spikes aligned with troughs
- strace -tt -p <executor_pid> during a trough -> bursts of short (1–3ms) nanosleep calls in dispatch path, unusually frequent context switches

Interesting log snippets:
- executor logs around drop:
  [2025-11-03T10:02:12Z] WARN  Batcher.cpp:412 prefill_wait_timeout (waited=61ms) batch_size=16 seq_len=128 route=hosted-eu
  [2025-11-03T10:02:12Z] INFO  KVCache.cpp:87 miss key=prefix:abc123
  [2025-11-03T10:02:12Z] INFO  ExecutorRing.cpp:233 consumed-batch id=2466 slots=12

- feeder logs (same time):
  [2025-11-03T10:02:11Z] DEBUG multiplexer.cpp:98 queued req_id=84321 latency_ms=2
  [2025-11-03T10:02:12Z] DEBUG multiplexer.cpp:121 dispatching batch_id=2466 target_size=16 assembled=12
  [2025-11-03T10:02:12Z] DEBUG multiplexer.cpp:129 prefill_sent=true

What stands out: feeder dispatches with target_size but assembled smaller batch. Batcher waits for prefill timeout then drains partial batch -> inefficient GPU pops. That aligns with our hypothesis of intermittent feeder speed variance. But why feeder stalls? Network/CPU?

Telemetry correlation:
- host-level: no OOMs, no node reboots.
- cgroup CPU throttling: none.
- process-level: high syscalls/sec during troughs, elevated context-switches/s
- GPU usage: stable but with small gaps (0.2–0.7s) between kernel submissions aligning to trough start times.
- KV cache metrics: miss rate spikes just before troughs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache miss storms cause executor to slow early token generation, increasing time to finish batches -> batcher times out and emits smaller batches.
   - Evidence: KV miss rate spike before troughs; Executor logs show 'miss key' and prefill wait.
   - Test: warm KV aggressively before traffic; add synthetic prefix-cache.
2) Feeder scheduling leads to short pauses (gc-like or blocking syscalls) under certain request patterns (long-tail prompts) causing dispatch jitter.
   - Evidence: feeder logs show occasional dispatches with smaller assembled size; strace shows nanosleep/syscalls.
   - Test: run feeder under perf and run workload with only short prompts vs mixed; observe variance.
3) Kernel-level thread affinity or cpuset oscillation causing context-switch thrashing between feeder and network thread.
   - Evidence: increased context switches; not yet confirmed.
   - Test: pin threads via taskset in canary.
4) Autoscaler scaling event in same node pool briefly changed network fabric -> small pause in RPCs.
   - Evidence: no autoscale events logged during initial incidents, so lower probability.

Quick experiments performed and results:
- Increased prefill timeout to 120ms on canary: trough depth reduced but throughput variance still present. (Mitigates but doesn't fix root cause.)
- Forced KV warmup (prefetch prefixes for top 10k keys) before load test: troughs significantly reduced in magnitude (tokens/s more stable). Strong signal for hypothesis #1.
- Run feeder with taskset to isolate on dedicated cores: slight improvement in trough frequency but not eliminated.

Action items (next):
- [ ] Add KV warm-start path for canary and observe 72h. If stable, push warm-start as opt-in for affected customers. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Add additional telemetry: per-request timestamps for prefill-sent vs prefill-ack, make those metrics available in Console with 1s granularity. (owner: Lin)
- [ ] Run a controlled experiment toggling feeder_thread_affinity=true/false on canary (owner: me)
- [ ] Add a small backlog-hold window: if assembled < target but KV miss rate > threshold, hold for extra 20ms before draining to give prefill a chance. Evaluate latency impact. (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] File a lightweight regression test that simulates KV-miss storm + mixed prompt lengths to catch this during pre-commit. (owner: CI team)

Questions / unresolved:
- Why does KV miss rate spike periodically? Is it due to cache eviction policy under certain request patterns or a upstream invalidation? Need to check invalidation logs.
- Is there any cross-tenant interference on shared cache backing store? Check metrics split by tenant.
- Are there any network retransmits (TCP) at times of trough? Add tcpdump sampling around trough window.

Notes to keep for the write-up to Eng Review:
- Include timeline plots: tokens/s, KV miss rate, GPU kernel submit timestamps, prefill wait timeout events.
- Show example request traces that cause a prefill miss chain (trace both feeder and executor).
- Recommend short-term mitigation (KV warm-start + small prefill hold) and long-term (cache policy tuning + stronger telemetry).

Random TTY commands I ran (for reproducibility):
- kubectl exec -it executor-canary -- bash -c "tail -n 1000 /var/log/executor.log | ts | grep prefill"
- go run tools/kv-prefetch/main.go --prefix-file /tmp/hot_prefixes.txt --target=10000
- ./loadtest --rps 450 --dist=short-only  # baseline
- ./loadtest --rps 450 --dist=mix-short-long --seed 42 # reproducer

Final quick note: warmup experiment gave me the highest confidence. If we can find why the cache gets cold in bursts, we can likely eliminate large portion of troughs without raising prefill timeout permanently.

-- Asha
